confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors come from two web searches. One was for the RBA rate. The other was a single combined price search that returned aggregate cost-of-living sites and a few venue menus, some dated 2023-2025. I converted CHF to USD at an assumed rate of roughly 1.25 USD per CHF. The searches gave rough Interlaken figures of CHF 4-5 for a cappuccino, CHF 7-10 for a 0.5 L draft beer, CHF 25 for a main-course lunch and CHF 117 for a mid-range dinner for two. A hotel bar menu put cocktails at CHF 19-22. Wine by the glass was poorly covered, so I based it on nearby mountain-village prices of CHF 7-10 per glass. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates, not based on any search or live listings. They are the least certain and assume July peak-season demand, when Interlaken prices are high and vary widely.
comparable_city_reasoning: Based on Swiss Alpine tourist-town price levels, comparing Interlaken with Zurich and nearby Lauterbrunnen. Interlaken is somewhat cheaper than Zurich for food but carries a strong peak-season premium on accommodation.
